family.name: Data Analyst
family.summary: A VP needs "which region grew most" for a board deck in an hour: find the double-loaded month and the cancelled order that flip the answer, decide what to send, and catch the maths mistakes in a teammate’s summary.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Which region grew most?
stages.summary: Answer a VP's question from a dashboard with a double-loaded month and a cancelled order that flip the answer. Think aloud.

stages.title: What do you send at 3 pm?
stages.summary: The VP needs a number for the board now; one fix isn't confirmed. Tests judgement under time pressure. Think aloud.

stages.title: The next morning
stages.summary: Consequences of what they sent. Tests ownership and fixing the root cause.

stages.title: Check a teammate's summary
stages.summary: A summary with an average of averages, percent confused with percentage points, and a 14-slice pie chart. Think aloud.

stages.title: The note to the VP (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the corrected regional summary with AI. Catches copied dashboard numbers and false precision.

stages.title: When the data was wrong
stages.summary: A real time they found or missed a data problem. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You're the data analyst at **Sutra Textiles**, which makes home textiles sold to retail stores. The VP of Sales messages at 2 pm: **"Which region grew the most from Q4 to Q1? I need it for the board deck by 3."**

brief.caption: Revenue by region from the sales dashboard (₹ lakh)

brief.text: Notes from the data engineering channel this quarter

items: East moved to a new billing system in February. "The February load might have run twice, still checking." East's February shows 99 (₹ lakh).
North booked a bulk order of 45 (₹ lakh) on 28 March. Finance cancelled it on 3 April; the dashboard only counts bookings, not cancellations.
West changed its region code from "W1" to "WEST" in January. The mapping was fixed the same week and backfilled.

brief.text: The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: How would you explain what an average hides to someone who isn’t into numbers?
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Which region really grew the most?** Show your working: what you adjusted, by how much, and how confident you are.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

stages.title: What do you send at 3 pm?

choices.label: Send the corrected numbers now, with the caveats stated
Send the dashboard numbers now and correct them later
Tell the VP you need until tomorrow to confirm with the data team
Send both versions and let the VP choose

prompt.text: It's 2:45 pm. The data team hasn't confirmed the February double-load yet. **What do you send the VP?** Pick one, then write the message (three or four lines).

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Send the corrected numbers now, with the caveats stated"

prompt.text: The data team confirms February ran twice. But the East regional manager is upset: "My bonus is tied to that dashboard. Who changed my numbers?" He has emailed the VP.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Send the dashboard numbers now and correct them later"

prompt.text: The deck went to the board saying East grew fastest. The data team has now confirmed February ran twice, so East's growth was overstated. The CFO asks who signed off the numbers.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Tell the VP you need until tomorrow to confirm with the data team"

prompt.text: The VP used the dashboard numbers anyway because nothing arrived by 3 pm. The double-load is now confirmed. The VP asks why you didn't just send your best estimate.
**What do you say and do?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Send both versions and let the VP choose"

prompt.text: The VP picked the dashboard version "because it looked better for East". The double-load is now confirmed.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: A teammate wrote this for the monthly review. **Find the problems, worst first, and say what each one gets wrong.**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

items: **Average order value is up 18%.** We took each region's average order value and averaged the four regions. The small East region's average rose 34%; North, our biggest region, was flat.
**Online share grew 5%**: from 12% of sales to 17%.
**Product mix:** see the pie chart with all 14 product categories.
Data covers every order from 1 to 31 March, pulled on 2 April.

stages.title: The note to the VP (AI allowed)

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write the note to the VP (under 150 words) with the corrected regional growth, what you changed and why, and what still needs confirming.

items: Paste your final answer.
Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Tell us about a time you found, or missed, a problem in data people were relying on.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
